Hi Javier,

Yes, if you run

rm -rf /Library/Frameworks/R.framework

it will delete any packages you installed with CRAN R and you'll need to reinstall them. Note that if you use "checkpoint" packages are installed locally to the project folder, so it won't affect any of those as you upgrade to new versions of RRO.

Making the version-to-version transition is something we aim to make easier with RRO, especially with regard to packages, so please keep the feedback and suggestions coming!

Hope this helps,
# David Smith

Hi, Alberto

Using the logical processors would make almost no difference in computing speed, other than possibly slowing down the overall performance.

The reason is this:
Parallel processing requires overhead of communication between cores, thus the overall performance increase is lower than the available parallel units.  See  Amdahls's law http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amdahl%27s_law
Hyperthreading works by buffering input/output and then switching a physical core to different computation tasks
For a high performance compute problem, e.g. matrix algebra, the I/O overhead is low and the compute task is large.
Consequently using logical cores will only decrease performance (Amdahl's law)
The MKL already optimizes your available parallel computing resource.  This is why I would not expect Intel to make any change to this architecture.

(Somebody please prove me wrong.)

Regards

Andrie

On the other hand, is there a way to switch off sourcing packages from mran, and maybe go back to a versioned environment later (e.g. during the final steps of testing)?

Is there any plans to bring MKL to OSX in the future?

Many thanks!

Enzo

messages.body_plain:
In our testing we've found that the Accelerate Framework provides about the same performance on Macs, so the current plan is to stick with it. Is there something in particular you were looking for from MKL?

# David Smith

On Friday, December 26, 2014 11:37:46 AM UTC-8, Enzo wrote:
> Thanks Sheri.  Are there any plans to bring MKL to OSX in the future?
>
> On Friday, December 26, 2014 7:30:34 PM UTC, Sheri Gilley wrote:
> > You are correct - see http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/news/#rro801:
> >
> > The Mac build has been reconfigured to use the Mac Accelerate Framework for multi-threaded computations. This provides comparable performance to the Intel MKL. (Windows and Linux platforms continue to use Intel MKL.)
> > As for the package repository, you can switch to a different date, use a different repository (such as CRAN) or use checkpoint().  See http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/faq/#change-repos for details.
> >
> >
> > On Thu, Dec 25, 2014 at 5:04 PM, Enzo <emart...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > I have installed and dis-installed RRO on a couple of apple macs I have and listened to the webinar on the product.  I find RRO really interesting but I am still confused by what it is really about.
> > > If I have to answer an elevator-type of question on RRO I would say in order (beyond the obvious source compatibility with R Cran):
> > > 1. It delivers intel MKL as open source on R
> > > 2. It provides a versioned package repository to increase stability and control with  mran.revolutionanalytics.com <http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/>
> > > 3. It allows to switch overnight to be under maintenance at a fee.
> > >
> > > The problem is that since RRO launch few things have happened:
> > > . The apple mac version was actually using the Accelerate Framework Reference, not MKL.
> > > . As a developer of a (shiny) analytical application to use a versioned package repository is a big pain  in the butt: I need to be able to test betas of packages; install from github etc.  The situation may be different when I am going in production in a couple of months.
> > >
> > > This means that RRO is "just" the ability to use RR support, provided that I use 1. and 2.  Correct?
> > >
> > > On the other hand, is there a way to switch off sourcing packages from mran, and maybe go back to a versioned environment later (e.g. during the final steps of testing)?
> > >
> > > Is there any plans to bring MKL to OSX in the future?

> > > Many thanks!

My file path is "C:\Users\admin\Desktop\Kaggle\dog_1_both_marked.csv"

sampleDataDir <- rxGetOption("Kaggle")
inputFile <- file.path("C:\Users\admin\Desktop\Kaggle\dog_1_both_marked.csv", "dog_1_both_marked.csv")
outputFile <- file.path(tempdir(), "basicClaims.xdf")
rxTextToXdf(inFile = inputFile, outFile = outputFile, overwrite = TRUE)
rxGetInfo(data = outputFile, getVarInfo = TRUE, numRows = 100000)
file.remove(outputFile)

Thanks,
Amit
